items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: We had Ziggy Elman, Charlie Teagarden, and a bunch of the studio guys, the lead alto, Blake Reynolds from Paramount, lead alto from Fox, Russ Cheever, a couple of the guys, Red Ballard and Bruce Squires who were the two trombones in Benny’s band, so we had one heck of a band down there.

ctx.x: Well I went on the road with him I think for eight weeks. I made $110 a week and I sent 80 home every week. I lived on 30 bucks, like a king. Anything I wanted to eat, anywhere I wanted to eat, hotels, the whole thing, 30 dollars. This is 1942. And then I got

drafted, and I mean luckily I got into an Army band. We had Ziggy Elman, Charlie Teagarden, and a bunch of the studio guys, the lead alto, Blake Reynolds from Paramount, lead alto from Fox, Russ Cheever, a couple of the guys, Red Ballard and Bruce Squires who were the two trombones in Benny’s band, so we had one heck of a band down there. We had a radio show every week and I got to write for it and also play. So I spent two years like that and then because I was healthy after they disbanded the band in 1944, why…

Okay, I was going to ask if you got overseas. I seems like most of the musicians that I’ve talked to made out pretty well during their military service, that they were able to keep their music up in some respects.
